newsitem.title: UK: Chronology of major IRA attacks since February 96.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of major IRA attacks since February 96.

text.p: British security forces were on alert on Sunday in case the IRA marked the first anniversary of its massive Docklands bomb with renewed violence.
The following is a chronology of major attacks by the Irish Republican Army in the year since it broke its ceasefire:

Feb 9, 1996 - Huge bomb rocks Docklands in London killing two and injuring 100, causing millions of pounds worth of damage. The blast came just minutes after Irish radio said it received a statement from the IRA saying its 17-month ceasefire was over.
Feb 18 - Explosion rips apart a bus in London's Aldwych, killing the bomber and injuring nine others.
Mar 9 - Bomb explodes near West Brompton underground station in London. No reports of injuries.
Apr 17 - Bomb explosion shakes The Boltons, fashionable part of the Earl's Court district in west London. No one injured.
Apr 24 - Bomb goes off beside London's Hammersmith bridge. No one injured.
June 15 - Van bomb explodes in shopping centre in Manchester injuring more than 200 people and causing millions of pounds worth of damage.
June 28, 1996 - In Germany, IRA attacks a British army barracks at Osnabrueck with mortar bombs, setting off an explosion but causing no injuries.
Oct 7 - IRA stages first bombing in Northern Ireland for more than two years, attacking British army headquarters at Lisburn, near Belfast. A soldier is killed and 30 other people injured.
Jan 6, 1997 - IRA fires rocket at main Belfast court building, injuring a policeman.
Jan 26 - Off-duty British soldier wounded in suspected IRA booby-trap bomb attack.
In early 1997, there have been a series of mortar and grenade attacks on army and police patrols in Northern Ireland, but no-one has been seriously injured.
